title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: Minor denied — due confidence is that praying for others pleases God and we obtain as far as he sees fit; stands with our doctrine and with Arminian
pass_a_gloss: But let us proceed unto the Minor, in which they say that the reprobation posited by us hinders that prayers cannot be offered unto God with due confidence. We deny this, and say that unto due confidence it suffices that we are certain this duty of praying for others pleases God, and that we shall obtain for them insofar as it shall have seemed good unto God, and shall have been agreeable unto the Divine glory. This confidence can stand equally with our doctrine, and with the Arminian. For they dare not deny that the decree of reprobation is everlasting and irrevocable, although they assert that it rests upon the everlasting foresight of human unbelief. It is certain therefore that Judas reprobated from eternity can by no prayers of others be led unto salvation, even that reprobation being posited which Arminius maintains.
pass_b_english: But let us take the Minor: they say the reprobation we posit blocks prayers from being offered to God with due confidence. We deny that. Due confidence needs only this: we are certain the duty of praying for others pleases God, and that we shall obtain for them insofar as God sees fit and as agrees with divine glory. That confidence stands as well with our doctrine as with the Arminian. For they dare not deny that the reprobation decree is eternal and irrevocable, though they say it rests on eternal foresight of human unbelief. So it is certain: Judas reprobated from eternity can by no others' prayers be led to salvation — even on the reprobation Arminius maintains.
source_text: Sed pergamus ad Minorem, in qua dicunt reprobationem a nobis positam impedire quo minus preces cum debita fiducia Deo offerantur. Nos hoc negamus, et dicimus ad debitam fiduciam sufficere, quod certi sumus hoc officium orandi pro aliis Deo placere, et nos pro illis impetraturos, quatenus Deo visum fuerit, ac Divinae gloriae fuerit consentaneum. Haec fiducia stare potest aeque cum nostra doctrina, ac cum Arminiana. Nam illi non audent negare decretum reprobationis esse aeternum et irrevocabile, quamvis asserant illud niti aeterna humanae infidelitatis praevisione. Certum itaque est, Judam ab aeterno reprobatum nullis aliorum precibus posse ad salutem perduci, vel posita illa reprobatione quam tuetur Arminius.
